## Correction — the first push was incomplete; the head now carries the commit the numbers were measured on

The reviewing seat caught this and is right. Recording it so the numbers in the
description are anchored to the tree that actually landed.

**What went wrong.** I pushed after the first commit, then made a second commit
(`7ae8cd8d86`, *count the census by MERGE, not by run*) and removed the worktree
before pushing it. The commit survived in the shared object database and the local
branch ref still pointed at it, so the fix was a plain fast-forward —
`d5ad2b97ed..7ae8cd8d86`. ⛔ No rebase, no amend, no force-push.

**Why it mattered rather than being bookkeeping.** The unpushed commit is the one
that changes the census unit from a RUN to a MERGE. On the old head `summarise()`
counted runs, which over this window yields 456/303 where objectui#6055 published
454/301. The by-sha collapse — which folds the four superseded runs objectui#6049's
per-sha concurrency group creates — is what lands both columns on objectui#6055's
figures to the unit, and that reproduction is the strongest single piece of evidence
in the census. It was not on the PR.

**The head now.**

| reading | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| branch tip | `d5ad2b97ed` | **`7ae8cd8d86`** |
| commits on the PR | 1 | **2** |
| additions / deletions / files | +544 / −0 / 3 | **+595 / −0 / 3** |

**Recomputed probe expectations, from the pushed head.** These now match the
description's section 6 exactly — they were never wrong, only ahead of what had been
pushed:

```
git diff --stat 6214db63f 7ae8cd8d86   =>  3 files changed, 595 insertions(+)

0333b1e9b18bbc5b3e68c4a84bfd71f11803463c0830d6f2d5e55b762827d71e  scripts/coverage-red-cause-census.mjs
57f470170775b4e68ae8a5c20e1a8af0143a2fb2d331c7d896faed316632b162  scripts/__tests__/coverage-red-cause-census.test.ts
12e1f45d7abd3d4e9b414f21cb98996b06874729ae2d39526c71a4f4d10cc78b  scripts/coverage-red-cause-suspects.json

git merge-base --is-ancestor d5ad2b97ed 7ae8cd8d86  =>  exit 0   (fast-forward, not a rewrite)
```

The unit decision is present at the pushed head: `supersededRuns` / `bySha` /
`THE UNIT IS A MERGE` appear 9 times in the script and `superseded` 3 times in the
pin test, where the old head had 0 and 0.

**Gate set re-run on the pushed head `7ae8cd8d86`**, in a fresh worktree checked out
from the branch (the earlier worktree was removed, which is how the push got lost;
this one is a clean checkout of exactly what the PR carries). Exit codes captured
before any pipe.

| gate | exit | verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| pin test | 0 | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / **`Tests 20 passed (20)`** / `Duration 454ms` |
| `Test (coverage shard 1/4)` — the push lane's own command | **0** | `blob report written to .vitest-reports/blob-1-4.json`, and nothing else — 1459 lines / 118 KB, **zero** lines of vitest test summary, 0 hits for `ELIFECYCLE` / `FAIL` / `Error:` |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 | — |
| `check-entry-guard --self-test` | 0 | `63 cases pass` |
| `check-entry-guard` | 0 | `91 scripts/ file(s) … 0 file(s) still hand-type one` |
| `check-lint-coverage` | 0 | `46/46 packages linted, 0 with outstanding errors` |
| `check-type-check-coverage` | 0 | `43/43 packages compile their tests` |
| `check-pre-install-import-graph` | 0 | `every non-relative leaf a node builtin` |
| `check-upstream-port-parity` | 0 | `3 ported file(s) match` |
| `check-vi-mock-override-shape` | 0 | `4836 tracked source file(s)` |
| `check-shell-escape-residue` | 0 | `0 occurrence(s) outside a fence` |
| `check-changeset-fixed` | 0 | `privatePackages declared` |
| `check-control-bytes` | 0 | `scanned 7369 tracked text file(s)` |
| `check-changeset-presence` | 0 | `no changeset is owed` |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | 0 | `NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) … none matched` |
| `eslint --no-inline-config` on the 2 new JS/TS files | 0 | 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| control-char sweep over the 3 new files | 1 | no control bytes |

Every verdict matches what the description already reports — that tree **is** the one
that was tested; it simply had not been pushed.

⭐ **The headline reproduction, re-run from the pushed head** (this is the reading the
missing commit carries, so it is the one worth showing here rather than asserting):

```
node scripts/coverage-red-cause-census.mjs --snapshot=snap-6055-window.json
{ "runs": 456, "merges": 454, "supersededRuns": 2, "delivered": 153, "red": 301, "redShare": 0.6630,
  "byCause": { "doc-links corpus walk (objectui#8419)": 196,
               "whole-repository scan (objectui#8479 / objectui#8380)": 54,
               "doc-links … + whole-repository scan …": 29,
               "unattributed": 22 } }

node scripts/coverage-red-cause-census.mjs --snapshot=snap-full-window.json
{ "runs": 700, "merges": 696, "supersededRuns": 4, "delivered": 353, "red": 343, "redShare": 0.4928, … }
```

**454 merges and 301 red** — objectui#6055's published figures, to the unit, in both
columns.

And the counterfactual is measured rather than asserted: the PREVIOUS head's script
was extracted from the object database (`git show d5ad2b97ed:scripts/…`) and run over
the identical snapshot. It answers

```
{ "merges": 456, "delivered": 153, "red": 303, "redShare": 0.6645,
  "byCause": { …, "unattributed": 24 } }
```

— 456/303 against objectui#6055's 454/301, with the two superseded runs landing in
`unattributed` (24 rather than 22) because nothing folded them. That is the gap the
missing commit closes, and it is why this was worth a push rather than a footnote.

The pin test still computes into **shard 1 of 4** on the pushed head (3001 specs), so
shard 1 remains the shard owed.


⛔ Nothing else about the change moved. No file content differs from what the
description reports; the only defect was that one of the two commits had not left
this machine.

## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9180. ⭐ And the round's most useful output is a correction to THIS SEAT'S REVIEW RULE

Head `7ae8cd8d86`, **33 checks, 0 red, 0 pending**, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `mergeable_state: clean`. Every reading below is this seat's own.

### ⭐ First: the delivery gap, and why 「review the diff, ⛔ not the report」 would NOT have caught it

The report said every gate, every census figure and all three probe hashes were taken on `7ae8cd8d86`. The PR carried **`d5ad2b97e`** — 1 commit, **+544**. Measured:

```
git log -1 7ae8cd8d86        → "count the census by MERGE, not by run", parent = d5ad2b97e
git merge-base --is-ancestor 7ae8cd8d86 d5ad2b97e   → NOT an ancestor
```

⇒ the reported sha was a **CHILD** of the pushed head — local-only, never pushed.

⚠️ ⛔ **Not cosmetic.** Reading both trees: `superseded` pushed **0** / unpushed **2**; `collapse` **0** / **1**; the diff replaces `runs.filter(r => !r.delivered)` with a `bySha` map and a per-sha collapse. ⇒ the PR as it stood would have answered **456 / 303**, not 454 / 301 — and the 「reproduces objectui#6055 to the unit」 claim, the strongest evidence in the whole census, was ⛔ **not on the PR**.

⭐ **This seat's standing rule is 「review against the DIFF, ⛔ never the report」 — and it sends you to the diff.** The diff on offer was `d5ad2b97e`: the **wrong tree**. The rule silently assumes the diff and the report are about the same thing. ⇒ amended, and it now runs **before** the diff is opened:

> **Verify the sha the report claims to describe IS the sha the PR carries** — `git ls-remote origin <branch>` against the PR's `head.sha`, plus `git merge-base --is-ancestor <reported> <head>` whenever a report names a sha.
> ⚠️ A reported sha that is a **descendant** of the head is the dangerous shape: it reads like a later revision and is **undelivered work**.
> ⭐ Free tells: the report's insertion count not matching the PR's `additions`; a probe hash that does not reproduce; **1 commit** on a PR whose narrative describes two stages.

Here all three tells were present — 595 vs 544, two of three hashes stale, one commit.

### ✅ The fix, verified independently

| check | reading |
|---|---|
| `git ls-remote` head | **`7ae8cd8d86`** |
| PR | **2 commits**, **+595/−0**, 3 files |
| `coverage-red-cause-census.mjs` sha256 | `0333b1e9b18bbc5b…` ✅ matches report |
| `…census.test.ts` sha256 | `57f470170775b4e6…` ✅ |
| `…suspects.json` sha256 | `12e1f45d7abd3d4e…` ✅ |
| collapse logic on the head | `superseded` **2** · `collapse` **1** · `bySha` **8** |

A plain fast-forward, ⛔ no rebase, ⛔ no amend, ⛔ no force. Correction comment `5636170917`.

⭐ **And the counterfactual was turned into a MEASUREMENT rather than a claim**: the previous head's script, extracted from the object database and run over the *identical* snapshot, answers **456 / 303**, with the two superseded runs landing in `unattributed` (24 vs 22). ⛔ That is not an argument that the missing commit mattered — it is the number.

⭐ The cause was named unprompted and it is the reusable half: `git worktree remove` ran **before** the branch was verified in sync with its remote. ⇒ **cleanup is gated on `git rev-parse HEAD` == `git ls-remote`, ⛔ never on 「the PR is open」.** Going into this seat's dispatch-order template.

### ✅ Every tree-readable premise re-derived here

`ci.yml:967` zeroes the shard thresholds · real thresholds **40 / 33 / 30 / 40** at `vitest.config.mts:487-492` · **9** occurrences of `needs.test-coverage.result == 'success'` · `testTimeout: 15000` at `:282` · the lane split at `:718` (`!= push`) and `:925` (`== push`) · `pnpm test --shard=` at `:838` versus `pnpm test:coverage --reporter=blob` at `:966` · and all three episode-edge subjects (`0203a29e9b` the doc-links hoist, `83d4fda160` the unused-deps hoist, `f7cf7e8a9f` the walk-growing fix). ⛔ Nothing missed.

### ⭐ Three corrections accepted, and all three change what the lane believes

**1. The 66 % is an EPISODE, ⛔ not a rate.** Red rate by segment, at merge granularity: **4.3 %** before the doc-links walk grew → **87.8 %** → **100 %** → **20.9 %** after both hoists. ⇒ 「two thirds of push-lane spend buys a verdict that means nothing」 and 「**82 of 125** runner-hours per day」 were true of 2026-09-05..09-09 and are **not true now**. ⭐ The hypothesis is confirmed at a high share **and** the standing cost figure is stale — **both**, ⛔ not one. The residual **20.9 %** is still ~5× the pre-episode baseline and is the number any follow-up gets priced on.

**2. The mechanism is MARGINAL, ⛔ not binary.** The card, triage and my claim all say 「green on every PR and red on every push」. Exact for one segment (45/45) and **wrong** for the other (238/271 = 87.8 %). At **2.48× / 2.56×** instrumented cost the walk sits **at** the bound, so runner load decides each run. ⇒ a remedy priced on 「deterministic」 would mis-predict **271 of the 316** merges in the episode.

**3. ⛔ My 「instrumentation is the only variable」 was wrong.** Four things differ between the lanes — `--coverage`, `--reporter=blob`, four threshold overrides, and the non-push lane's `should_run` gate plus `pnpm test:dist` on shard 1. Only the first changes execution cost, so the conclusion survives; the phrasing does not. ⚠️ And I omitted that **`merge_group` is a second uninstrumented lane** — which is the only reason the empirical control exists at all: segment B shard 2 reads **0/358** on merge_group against **229/271** on push, with control shards that do not carry the suspect agreeing to within two points.

### ⭐ Why the attribution is a measurement and not an inference

⛔ No run was classified 「this mechanism」 because it was red and something was slow. Attribution requires **both** the suspect's live window **and** the computed shard, and the discriminating form is **cross-segment**: the suspect's shard never moves while its failure rate does — shard 2 runs 0.9 % → **84.5 %** → 8.9 % → 12.2 %, rising at the walk-growing commit and collapsing at the hoist. ⭐ And the second instance's onset is the file's own arrival: `check-unused-dependencies.test.ts` is added at 09:34:10Z and the first shard-1-red merge is **eighteen minutes later**.

⭐ **The round also said plainly where its own evidence is weak** — that the per-run shard test approaches circularity when one shard dominates a segment, and that a third instance in the 20.9 % residual is **NOT MEASURED** and ⛔ 「not 'no'」, because all eight candidates land on the same marginal rates and the test has no discriminating power there. ⇒ a measurement returning 「cannot tell」, ⛔ not a finding of absence.

### ⚠️ The finding that may matter more than the census

**objectui#9177**, filed bare: a red coverage shard **never says which test failed**. `--reporter=blob` prints one line, and the blob artifact is download-only. Demonstrated rather than asserted — a throwaway file with one failing assertion and one deliberate timeout, run both ways: the default reporter names both tests; `--reporter=blob` emits `blob report written to …` and nothing else. ⇒ **that is why both episodes had to be found by a human reading a job log days later**, and ⛔ nobody — not the card, not triage, not this seat — had named it.

⇒ **ACCEPT.** Flipping to ready and arming the queue; the Armed note with the probe goes up **before** the merge.

## Armed — `SQUASH`, merge queue entered. ⭐ Probe written HERE, ⛔ before the merge

`added_to_merge_queue` confirmed. Head `7ae8cd8d86` — **the corrected head**, ⛔ not the one the first push left. **33 checks, 0 red, 0 pending**; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` **success post-flip**.

⚠️ This note says **what CI reported**, ⛔ never 「required」: the branch-protection set is a repository-SETTINGS surface this repo cannot read, and its own classifier records a merge that happened with all four shards `in_progress`.

⭐ **TREE READS ONLY.** ⛔ No runner leg — this seat reviews from a bare checkout with no `node_modules` and cannot execute one; the runner readings below are the round's, marked as such.

```bash
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git fetch origin main -q
C=scripts/coverage-red-cause-census.mjs
T=scripts/__tests__/coverage-red-cause-census.test.ts
J=scripts/coverage-red-cause-suspects.json

echo "── SHAPE — the merge commit's OWN diff ──"
git diff --shortstat <MERGE_SHA>^ <MERGE_SHA>          # expect: 3 files changed, 595 insertions(+)
git diff --name-only <MERGE_SHA>^ <MERGE_SHA>          # expect: exactly those three paths

echo "── BYTES — the three files, hashed ──"
for f in "$C" "$T" "$J"; do printf '%-56s %s\n' "$f" "$(git show origin/main:$f | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)"; done
# expect  0333b1e9b18bbc5b / 57f470170775b4e6 / 12e1f45d7abd3d4e

echo "── THE COMMIT THAT WAS ALMOST LOST — the by-sha collapse must be present ──"
printf 'superseded=%s collapse=%s bySha=%s\n' \
  "$(git show origin/main:$C | grep -ci superseded)" \
  "$(git show origin/main:$C | grep -ci collapse)" \
  "$(git show origin/main:$C | grep -c bySha)"        # expect 2 / 1 / 8
git show origin/main:$C | grep -c 'runs.filter'        # expect 0 — the run-counting form is GONE

echo "── PIN FLOOR ──"
git show origin/main:$T | grep -cE '^\s*it\('          # floor 20

echo "── SURVIVED — the premises the census rests on, untouched ──"
git grep -n 'coverage.thresholds.lines=0' origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci.yml   # ci.yml:967
git grep -c "needs.test-coverage.result == 'success'" origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci.yml   # 9
git grep -n 'testTimeout' origin/main -- vitest.config.mts                          # :282  15000
git grep -n "if: github.event_name == 'push'" origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci.yml  # :925
```

### Expected, and where each comes from

| leg | expect | read from |
|---|--:|---|
| merge-commit diff | **3 files, 595 insertions** | ⭐ scoped to `<MERGE_SHA>^ <MERGE_SHA>`, ⛔ never a range ending at a moving ref |
| `census.mjs` · `census.test.ts` · `suspects.json` | `0333b1e9b18bbc5b` · `57f470170775b4e6` · `12e1f45d7abd3d4e` | hashed off the pushed head by this seat |
| `superseded` / `collapse` / `bySha` | **2 / 1 / 8** | ⭐ **the delivery leg** |
| `runs.filter` | **0** | ⭐ the run-counting form the lost commit replaced |
| `it(` call sites in the pin | floor **20** | and the round's runner says `Tests 20 passed (20)` ⇒ ⭐ **they agree, so no `.each` is hiding cases** |
| the four premise sites | unchanged | the census is only as good as these |

⭐ **Rows 3 and 4 are the point of this probe.** The first push carried a head that counted **runs**, and would have answered **456 / 303** instead of **454 / 301** — proved by running that exact script over the same snapshot. ⇒ a leg asking only 「did the files land?」 goes green on the wrong tree. **`superseded=2` and `runs.filter=0` are what distinguish the delivered head from the one that was almost merged.**

⚠️ Row 5 pairs a tree read with a runner reading **taken by the round, ⛔ not by this seat** — recorded that way because a count of `it(` call sites is ⛔ not a test count when `.each` is present. Here it is, and they agree at 20; that agreement is the control.
